lawyer:
Fida M Kamal, Senior Advocate with Zainul Abedin, Senior Advocate, Anowarul Azim Khayer, with AM Aminuddin, with Khairul Alam, and Sagir Hossain, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Abdul Baset Majumder Senior Advocate with Yusuf Hossain Humayan, Senior Advocate, Hassan MS Azim, and M Sayed Ahmed, Advocates ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Nazrul Islam Khan (Md) ------- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Dhaka and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 9-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 5 in Election Appeal No. 01 of 2014 (Annexure-E) dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the order dated 4-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 6 (Annexure-C) cancelling the nomination paper of the petitioner shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and further to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to accept the nomination paper filed by the petitioner to contest in the election for the post of Upazila Chairman, Nazirpur, Pirojpur scheduled to be held on 27-2-2014 and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the petitioner in short is that the petitioner as being a permanent citizen of the Nazirpur Upazila under Pirojpur with an intention to participate in the 4th Upazila Election submitted nomination paper on 2-2-2014 with necessary papers and documents as per Local Government (Upazila Parishad) Ain, 1998 by swearing affidavit with all particulars as per notification as a candidate to participate the election for the post of Upazila Chairman, Nazirpur, Pirojpur. The petitioner also submitted tax return for the year 2013-2014 with other papers. In the writ petition it has been also stated that one MA Malek Bepary a rival candidate of the petitioner filed an objection on 4-2-2014 against the petitioner stating that in the nomination paper the petitioner has not mentioned that he has some loan with the Bank. It is also stated in the writ petition that the respondent No. 6 after examining and scrutinizing the candidature of the petitioner cancelled his nomination paper on 4-2-2014 stating that he has not filed the tax return, the description of his property, the redemption from debts, his professional certificate and also the signature of the supporter was not found valid. The petitioner being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated 2-2-2014 preferred Election Appeal No. 01/ Pirojpur/14 before the respondent No. 5 on 6-2-2014. Subsequently, the said appeal was heard by the Deputy Commissioner, Pirojpur, the respondent No. 5. The election appeal authority of District Pirojpur without considering the relevant law and without proper appreciation of the papers and documents dismissed the appeal by its order dated 9-2-2014 and affirmed the order passed by the Returning Officer. Against the said order the petitioner filed this writ petition and obtained Rule. In the Rule issuing order it was mentioned that "the petitioner is directed to get the Rule heard and disposed of within one year from date in default the Rule shall stand discharged" and it was also mentioned in the Rule issuing order that "however the fate of the petitioner will be subject to the outcome of the Rule."

3. In the meantime, the election took place on 27-2-2014 the petitioner participated in the said election and got elected. On 9-3-2014 a gazette notification was published declaring the petitioner as the Chairman of Nazirpur Upazila Parishad, Pirojpur and he has been functioning as the Upazila Chairman Nazirpur till this date. It appears from the record that the petitioner on 23-2-2015 filed an application before a Bench comprising their Lordships Mr Justice Shamim Hasnain and Mr Justice Mohammad Ullah for modification of the order dated 11-2-2014 passed by a Division Bench of this Court, the modification was sought by way of an extension of the order of direction or by granting direction a fresh. The order sought to be modified was the Rule issuing order. Their Lordships after hearing the application rejected the same as according to them there was no scope for modification of the Rule issuing order. Against the said order passed by this Court the petitioner filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal being No. 634 of 2015 before the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which was ultimately rejected as being not pressed on 13-4-2015. On the basis of the order dated 13-4-2015 passed by the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the order dated 23-2-2015 passed by this Court, the respondents-government declared the post of Upazila Chairman of Nazirpur, Pirojpur vacant vide gazette notification dated 24-8-2015. Thereafter, on 7-9-2015 the petitioner filed an application for restoration of the instant Rule which was discharged ipso facto after expiry of 1 (one) year from the date of Rule issuing order i.e. from 11-2-2014. This application was heard by their Lordships Mr Justice Mirza Hussain Haider and Mr Justice AKM Zahirul Hoque. After elaborate hearing their Lordships rejected the said application observing that—"From the chronology of foots it appears that upon obtaining interim order the petitioner contested the election and was elected as the Chairman. Thereafter, pursuant to the Rule being discharged the office of the said Chairman has been declared vacant by the Election Commissioner. Thus the cause of action of this Rule as to cancellation of nomination paper in the election dated 27-2-2014 is no more subsisting. With the declaration of fresh election schedule on 2-9-2015 the entire election process though bye-election has been made open to everybody. As such, all the intending candidates, including the petitioner, are at liberty to contest the said election by filing their nomination papers afresh, as appears from Annexure-12 to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 7. Thus, whether the petitioner's nomination paper for the election doted 27-2-2014 was illegally cancelled or not is no more subsisting.

4. Under such circumstances, we do not find any merit in this application.

5. Accordingly, the application for restoration is hereby rejected.

6. Thereafter, the petitioner filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal being No. 2747 of 2015 before the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and their Lordships after hearing both the parties were pleased to pass the following order:

"This petition is directed from a judgment of the High Court Division by which it rejected the application for restoration in Writ Petition No. 1392 of 2014. We have perused the impugned judgment and other materials on record. Heard the learned Counsel of both the parties, in view of the submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the High Court Division erred in law in refusing the application for restoration. We find merit of the submission of the learned Counsel. The judgment of the High Court Division is set-aside.

The Writ Petition No. 1392 of 2014 is restored to its original file and number. Let the rule in Writ Petition No. 1392 of 2014 be heard and dispose of by the High Court Division on merit Bench presided over by Obaidul Hassan, J by 15th December, 2015. The parties, if so advised, may take steps in this regard. The leave petition is accordingly, disposed of with the above observation.

7. Then the petitioner appearing before this Bench filed an application for a supplementary Rule challenging the gazette notification dated 24-8-2015 by which the post of the Chairman of Nazirpur Upazila Parishad, Pirojpur was declared vacant. After hearing the said application this Bench issued a supplementary Rule in the following terms: "a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the gazette notification being No. 46.046. 027.00. 00421.2014-996 dated 24-8-2015 (Annexure-X) should not be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

8. This bench also fixed the matter on 8-12-2015 for hearing of the said writ petition as per the direction of the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

9. Mr Fida M Kamal the learned senior advocate appearing along with Mr Zainul Abedin, the learned senior advocate, Mr Anowarul Azim Khayer, Mr AM Aminuddin, Mr Khairul Alam and Mr Md Sagir Hossain, the learned advocates on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner filed two nomination papers one nomination paper has been dealt with and has been rejected by the Returning Officer and another nomination paper was not dealt with. The appellate authority i.e. the respondent No. 5, Deputy Commissioner, Pirojpur has also dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the Returning Officer, but in disposing the appeal he observed that –“জনাব নজরুল ইসলাম অপর একটি মনোনয়ন পত্র দাখিল করেন যার সমর্থনকারী মোঃ ইয়াহিয়া খান। বিজ্ঞ রিটার্নিং অফিসার আপীলকারীর ২য় মনোনয়ন পত্রের বিষয়ে আদেশে কিছু উল্লেখ করেননি যা যথাযথ নয়।” Mr Fida M Kamal submits that the rejection of single nomination paper does not automatically invalidate the other nomination paper as per Rule 17(A) of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013. He further submits that as per the Rule 15(6) each and every candidate is entitled to file more than one nomination paper and it is the foremost duty of the Returning Officer to deal with all the nomination papers. In this present case rejection of a single nomination paper of the petitioner has not invalidated the other nomination paper which has not been dealt with by the Returning Officer and, as such, the petitioner is/was a valid candidate for the Upazila Election of Nazirpur under Pirojpur District. He further submits that after issuance of the Rule the petitioner participated in the election and got elected and gazette notification has been published declaring him elected Chairman of Nazirpur Upazila Parisand under the Pirojpur District on 9-3-2014 and till this date he has been functioning as the Upazila Chairman. He further submits that although he tried to get the Rule heard as per the condition of the Rule issuing order within 1 (one) year from the date of issuing of the Rule, but due to pre-occupation of the Benches of the High Court Division the Rule could not be heard in time. He further submits that though the petitioner unsuccessfully took initiative to get the Rule heard within the time, but it was also the responsibility of the election commission, the respondent No. 2 and others to take initiative to get the Rule heard in time, but they did not come forward to get the Rule heard and they waited for passing time.

10. Mr Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned senior advocate appeared along with Mr Yusuf Hossain Humayan, the learned senior advocate, Mr Hassan MS Azim and Mr M Sayed Ahmed the learned advocates on behalf of the respondent No. 7. Though a good number of lawyers appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 7, but the main argument was advanced by Mr Hassan MS Azim and Mr M Sayed Ahmed Mr Hassan MS Azim, the learned advocate submits that it was the condition precedent to the Rule issuing order to get the Rule heard within one year from the date of issuance of the said order and it was also mentioned in the Rule issuing order that 'the fate of the petitioner will be subject to the outcome of the Rule.' Since the petitioner could not get the Rule heard in time as per the condition of the Rule issuing order itself, the Rule has been discharged automatically. He further submits that the writ petition itself is not maintainable as the petitioner has come before this Court against the rejection of his nomination paper. He further submits that as per Rule 17(4) of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 the Returning Officer will have to either accept or reject any nomination paper and in this case he has rejected the petitioner's nomination paper. In reply to the submissions of the learned advocate Mr Fida M Kamal regarding another nomination paper which has not been dealt with by the Returning Officer, Mr Azim submits that as per Rule 19 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 the Returning Officer has published the list of valid candidates in which the petitioner's name did not get any place, it means the petitioner's none of the nomination papers was accepted by the Returning Officer. In support of his submission Mr Azim referred decisions in the case of Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 425, AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Huq, reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68 and also in the case of AKM Mayeedul Islam vs Bangladesh Election Commission reported in 48 DLR (AD) 208. Citing those decisions Mr Azim submits that it is well settled that the writ petition is not maintainable against any step in the process of election like acceptance or rejection of nomination paper of a candidate and, as such, the writ petition itself is not maintainable.

11. In reply to the argument advanced by Mr Azim, Mr Fida M Kamal submits that the question of maintainability was raised before the Appellate Division by the respondent No. 7 at the time of hearing of the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2747 of 2015, but their Lordships in the Appellate Division did not accept their submissions and restored the Rule to its original file and number which indicates the question of maintainability of filing of the writ petition against rejection of a nomination paper has not been accepted by the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. He further submits that in the case of AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Huq reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68 the Appellate Division dealt with the Union Parishad Election matter. In the aforesaid case their Lordships dealt with 9 Civil Appeals and one Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal, but in all the cases election took place and after the election is over the petitioners came before this Court challenging the decision of the Election Commission. In those cases their Lordships observed that—"The jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution cannot be invoked except on the very limited ground of total absence of jurisdiction (coram non-judice) or malice in law to challenge any step in the process of election including an order passed by the Election Commission under Rule 70 because (a) the real and larger issue of completion of free and fair election with rigorous promptitude for timely emergence and functioning of elected bodies must take precedence over settlement of private disputes, (b) all election disputes must wait pending completion of the election and be taken to the special forum created under the Election Law itself for their resolution, (c) almost invariably there will arise dispute over facts which cannot and should not be decided in an extraordinary and summary jurisdiction of writ." Mr Fida M Kamal further submits that the essence of the said judgment is not to interfere with the election commission's decision as the Election Commission is the authority according to Rule 70 of the Union Parishad Election Rules, 1983 (now omitted) to determine whether the election was held honestly, justly and fairly by considering the evidence, but sitting in the writ jurisdiction there is no any scope to ascertain any evidence, but in the present case the question of rejection of nomination paper has been dealt with by the High Court Division. In this regard, Mr Fida M. Kamal focussed to the provisions of filing of nomination paper and some other provision as has been mentioned in the Upazila Parishad Ain, 1998 and Rules there under. As per Upazila Parishad Ain, 1998 the Tribunal is empowered to deal with the election dispute as per section 22(Ka). He referred section 22(Ka)(3) where it has been stated that only the valid candidates can go to the Tribunal. He also referred Rule 55 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 where it has been stated that only a contesting candidate can file an election dispute application before the Tribunal. Since the petitioner's nomination paper has been rejected and the appellate authority affirmed the order of the Returning Officer which is as per Rule 18(4) of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 is final, the petitioner did not have any other forum to move other than to invoke the writ jurisdiction of this Court and thus the present case is quite distinguishable from the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68. He further submits that in the case of Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is also not similar to the present case, Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir was convicted and his nomination paper was rejected and ultimately he preferred an appeal before the appellate authority and the order of Returning Officer was upheld by the appellate authority for the reason that at the time of filing of the nomination paper the petitioner was not found as a valid candidate to contest the poll as he was convicted by the competent Court of law for criminal offences. On the other hand, in the case in our hand the petitioner's one nomination paper was dealt with although the allegations raised by the respondent No. 7 were not properly inquired by the Returning Officer before rejecting the said nomination paper. But nevertheless the 2nd nomination paper was not at all dealt with by the Returning Officer and, as such, the 2nd nomination paper can be considered as the valid nomination paper and the petitioner has/had right to contest the election but when in the list of the candidates the petitioner's name did not get place he moved before this Court. The facts of the two cases are also quite distinguishable. He further submits that in the case of AKM Mayeedul Islam vs Bangladesh Election Commission reported in 48 DLR (AD) 208 the Returning Officer accepted the nomination paper of Hossain Mohammad Ershad, against that order of acceptance the petitioner came before this Court where their Lordships held the same view as the view expressed in 41 DLR (AD) 68. Mr Fida M Kamal further submits that the spirit of 48 DLR is to allow the "ball to role on the ground". In the present case, the High Court Division at the time of issuing Rule has taken the same view that the election process of the Nazirpur Upazila should not be halted and the man who came before the Court should be allowed to contest the election. The petitioner getting this order from this Court contested the election and the people at large of Nazirpur who are the ultimate judges of the fate of the election runners decided in favour of the petitioner and elected him as the Upazila Chairman of Nazirpur under District Pirojpur. He further submits that as per condition of the Rule the same automatically stood discharged on 10-2-2015 after elapse of one year. The post of the Upazila Parishad Nazirpur, Pirojpur was declared vacant by the respondents. But considering all these facts their Lordships in the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court restored the Rule to its original file and number which means our Apex Court in anyway did not want to halt the election process. He further submits that it was also the duty of the respondent like the petitioner to fix the Rule in time and to get the matter, heard as it has got public importance, but the respondents particularly the Election Commission did not take any step to get the matter heard in time. He further submits that today also the election commission has not come to the Court to contest the Rule. The respondent No. 7 was defeated by the petitioner. He is trying to unseat petitioner from the post of Upazila Chairman raising some technical questions. He further submits that if the petitioner would be defeated in the election he could have gone to the Election Tribunal but since he was not allowed by the respondents to contest the poll and there is no any forum after appeal was disposed of by the appellate authority, he rightly moved this Court under writ jurisdiction because a citizen of the country cannot remain remedy less. He also submits that after election is over the respondent No. 7 could go to the Election Tribunal for a declaration that the election of the petitioner is void or whole of the election process is void as per provision of Rule 61 of Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013, but without filing any petition before the Tribunal the respondent No. 7 sat idle and waited till elapsing one year from the date of issuance of the Rule. In the meantime the petitioner was put in jail. Despite being elected the petitioner could not run the Upazila properly, because of obstruction created by the respondent No. 7 on this or that plea. Finally Mr Fida M Kamal submits that since the petitioner was allowed to participate in the election by this Court and has been elected by the people of his locality and has been discharging his duties in spite of many obstructions created by the respondent No. 7, he should not be thrown on the street for some technical reasons which are not acceptable as per law and as such he prays for making the Rule absolute.

12. We have gone through the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition, application for supplementary Rule and annexures annexed thereto and other materials on record. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates for both the sides and the decision cited by the learned advocates. We have also gone through the relevant laws. It appears that the petitioner filed two nomination papers to contest the election of Upazila Parishad of Nazirpur under Pirojpur District. After filing nomination paper an objection was filed by the respondent No. 7 regarding validity of the nomination paper of the petitioner. The Returning Officer considering the objection rejected one nomination paper of the petitioner, but he did not take any decision regarding the petitioner's other nomination paper. Even the Returning Officer did not say anything whether he examined the 2nd nomination paper. Since one nomination paper was rejected the petitioner preferred an appeal before the appellate authority i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Pirojpur, the respondent No. 5. The appellate authority after hearing both sides upheld the decision of the Returning Officer but in giving his decision he observed that “বিজ্ঞ রিটার্নিং অফিসার আপীলকারীর ২য় মনোনয়ন পত্রের বিষয়ে আদেশে কিছু উল্লেখ করেননি যা যথাযথ নয়।” It appears that one nomination paper was rejected by the Returning Officer on some grounds, though the petitioner's case is that these are not the valid reasons for rejection of the nomination paper. However, amongst those reasons one reason was the signature of the seconder Shamim Hassan was not found valid, but in the 2nd nomination paper as submitted by the petitioner the seconder's name was Nazrul Islam. Now the question is whether cancelling one nomination paper automatically renders the 2nd nomination paper of the petitioner invalid. Rule 15 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 deals with the filing of nomination paper. In Rule 15(6) it has been mentioned that “কোন ব্যক্তি একই নির্বাচনী এলাকার জন্য একাধিক মনোনয়নপত্র দাখিল করিতে পারিবেন।” Rule 17 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules deals with the scrutiny of the nomination paper. Accordingly as per Rule 17(3) the Returning Officer has the power to reject any nomination paper if it is found that the said nomination paper is not valid in the eye of law. The provision of Rule 17(3) of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 runs as follows:

“(৩) রিটার্নিং অফিসার স্বীয় উদ্যোগে অথবা উপ-বিধি (১) এ উল্লিখিত কোন ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক উপ-বিধি (২) এর অধীন উত্থাপিত আপত্তির প্রেক্ষিতে তদবিবেচনায় সংক্ষিপ্ত তদন্ত পরিচালনা করিতে পারিবেন এবং কোন মনোনয়ন বাতিল করিতে পারিবেন, যদি তিনি সন্তুষ্ট হন যে,

(ক) প্রার্থী চেয়ারম্যান বা ক্ষেত্রমত ভাইস চেয়ারম্যান, মহিলা ভাইস চেয়ারম্যান বা মহিলা সদস্য হিসাবে মনোনীত হইবার যোগ্য নহেন; বা

(খ) প্রস্তাবকারী বা সমর্থনকারী মনোনয়নপত্রে স্বাক্ষর করিবার যোগ্য নহেন; বা

(গ) বিধি ১৫ বা ক্ষেত্রমত বিধি ১৬ এর কোন বিধান পালন করা হয় নাই; বা

(ঘ) প্রস্তাবকারী বা সমর্থনকারীর স্বাক্ষর নহে; বা

(ঙ) বিধি ১৫ এর উপ-বিধি (৩) এর দফা (গ) এর উপ-দফা (ঈ) এর অধীন হলফনামা দাখিল করা হয় নাই বা দাখিলকৃত হলফনামায় অসত্য তথ্য প্রদান করা হইয়াছে বা অসম্পূর্ণ তথ্য প্রদান করা হইয়াছে বা হলফনামায় উল্লেখিত কোন তথ্যের সমর্থনে যথাযথ সার্টিফিকেট, দলিল ইত্যাদি দাখিল করা হয় নাইঃ তবে শর্ত থাকে যে,

(অ) বাতিলকৃত কোন মনোনয়নপত্র কোন প্রার্থীর বৈধ মনোনয়নপত্রকে অবৈধ করিবে না;

(আ) রিটার্নিং অফিসার গুরুতর নহে, যেমন প্রার্থীর বা প্রস্তাবকারীর বা সমর্থনকারীর বা ভোটার এলাকার বা নির্বাচনী এলাকার নামের বানান ভুল অথবা তাহাদের কাহারো পরিচিতি নম্বর বা ভোটার নম্বর ত্রুটিপূর্ণ হইলে, এইরুপ কোন ত্রুটির কারণে কোন মনোনয়নপত্র বাতিল করিবেন না এবং অনুরুপ ত্রুটি তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে সংশোধন করিবার জন্য সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবেন; এবং

(ই) রিটার্নিং অফিসার ভোটার তালিকায় লিপিবদ্ধ কোন বিষয়ের শুদ্ধতা বা বৈধতা সম্পর্কে তদন্ত করিতে পারিবেন না। নিষ্পত্তি করিবেন।”

13. The appellate authority hears the appeal under the provision of Rule 18, the decision of the appellate authority has been made final by the said Rule. The relevant portion of the Rule 18(4) of Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 runs as follows:

“(৪) মনোনয়নপত্র গ্রহণ বা বাতিলের বিরুদ্ধে আপীল, সরাসরি অথবা যেরুপ প্রয়োজনীয় বলিয়া বিবেচিত হইবে সেইরুপ সংক্ষিপ্ত তদন্তের পর উহা দায়েরের তারিখ হইতে ৩ (তিন) দিনের মধ্যে নিষ্পত্তি করিতে হইবে এবং অনুরুপ আপীলের ক্ষেত্রে গৃহীত সিদ্ধান্ত চূড়ান্ত হইবে।” and thereafter vide Rule 19 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 the Returning Officer will publish a list of valid candidates. The provision of Rule 19 runs as follows:

“(১৯)। বৈধ প্রার্থীর তালিকা প্রকাশঃ (১) রিটার্নিং অফিসার বিধি ১৭ এর অধীন মনোনয়নপত্র বাছাইয়ের পর, বৈধভাবে মনোনীত প্রার্থীগণের প্রাথমিক তালিকা প্রস্তুত ও প্রকাশ করিবেন।

(২) বিধি ১৮ এর অধীনে যদি কোন আপীল দায়ের করা হইয়া থাকে, তবে উক্ত আপীলের উপর সিদ্ধান্ত প্রাপ্তির পর ফরম “গ” তে বৈধভাবে মনোনীত প্রার্থীগণের তালিকা প্রস্তুত করিয়া তাঁহার অফিসের নোটিশ বোর্ডে প্রকাশ করিবেন।”

14. It appears from Rule 15(6) of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 that any candidate has a right to file more than one nomination paper. According to Rule 17(4) the Returning Officer will examine each and every nomination paper and he has power to accept or reject any nomination paper, but he shall have to give reason for his decision. But in this case it appears that the Returning Officer failed to examine the 2nd nomination paper of the petitioner. As per Rule 17(3)(অ) if one nomination paper of a candidate is rejected it does not make the other nomination paper invalid and thus the non-examination of the 2nd nomination paper by the Returning Officer is a clear violation of law and it does not ipso facto make the 2nd nomination paper of the petitioner invalid. Further, it is the petitioner's case that on the basis of objection raised by the respondent No. 7 regarding the 1st nomination paper of the petitioner the Returning Officer without holding any inquiry or investigation came to a decision rejecting the petitioner's nomination paper. It appears from the Annexure-C of the writ petition (the rejection order by the Returning Officer) that the Returning Officer has rejected one nomination paper of the petitioner on the basis of an objection raised by the respondent No. 7, but there is no any reflection in the order that the Returning Officer, the respondent No. 7 has ever held any inquiry or investigation regarding the objection raised by the respondent No. 7.

15. Now let us see what was the contents of Rule issuing order. The Rule issuing order has two parts; 1st part is "to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 9-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 5 in Election Appeal No. 1 of 2014 (Annexure-E) dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the order dated 4-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 6 (Annexure-C) cancelling the nomination paper of the petitioner shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect."

16. And the 2nd portion is "to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to accept the nomination paper filed by the petitioner to contest in the election for the post of Upazila Chairman, Nazirpur, Pirojpur scheduled to be held on 27-2-2014 and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." It appears from the writ petition that the petitioner challenged the action of the respondents on two counts; No. 1 he challenged the decision dated 9-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 5 in Election Appeal No. 1 of 2014 dismissing the appeal and affirming the order dated 4-2-2014 passed by the respondent No. 4 the Returning Officer cancelling the nomination paper of the petitioner and other part was for a direction upon the respondents not to disqualify the petitioner to allot the electoral symbol for the post of Upazila Chairman of Nazirpur, Pirojpur. Considering the prayer of the writ petitioner this Court passed the 2nd part of the Rule issuing order and asked the respondents to allow the petitioner to participate in the election. It is very clear from the Rule issuing order that their Lordships could have stayed the decision passed by the respondent No. 5 in disposing the Election Appeal of the petitioner, but they did not stay the operation of the order of the respondent No. 5 dated 9-2-2014, rather they have passed the 2nd part of the Rule issuing order and directed the respondents to allow the petitioner to contest the election. We are of the view that since the respondent No. 6, the Returning Officer did not give any decision regarding the 2nd nomination paper the High Court Division at the time of the issuance of the Rule correctly directed the respondents to allow the petitioner to participate in the election. According to Mr Azim as per provision of Rule 19 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 the Returning Officer, the respondent No. 6 published the names of the valid candidates, meaning thereby the candidature of the petitioner was not found in order and also it is implied that the 2nd nomination paper has also been rejected. We are not inclined to accept the argument advanced by Mr Azim because as per Rule 17 (4) the each and every nomination paper is to be examined and considered by the Returning Officer before he publishes the list of the valid candidates under the provision of rule 19. It is also in Rule 17(3)(A) that if one nomination paper is rejected it does not automatically invalidate the other nomination paper filed. The Returning Officer must examine each and every nomination paper filed by any candidate. Since the 2nd nomination paper of the petitioner was not examined by the Returning Officer and no decision whatsoever was given on that nomination paper, we are of the view that the 2nd nomination paper was a valid nomination paper which qualified the petitioner to participate in the election. Mr Azim in support of his submission referred three decisions, mainly he emphasized on the decision of the case of Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 425. This case is not identical to the case in hand. In this case the petitioner was convicted by a competent Court of law under section 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and was sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for 3 years under section 26(2) and rigorous imprisonment for 10 years under section 27(1) and to pay a fine of Taka 10,00,000 under the said Act, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 1 (one) year respectively by the Special Judge. Court No. 3, in Special Case No. 1 of 2007.

17. He preferred Appeal before this Court being Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 and the appellant in that case was enlarged on bail and the sentence of fine was stayed, but the appeal did not reach to its finality, which means the appeal was not heard. In the circumstances, Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir's nomination paper was rejected by the Returning Officer and he challenged the same before this Court and this Court did not entertain the same. The decision of the Appellate Division in the said case does not apply to the case in hand because here the petitioner's nomination paper was rejected on the ground of giving improper statement in the Halafnama and the signature of the seconder was not found correct and valid, but the Returning Officer arrived at his decision without holding any inquiry or investigation as required under the provision of Rule 17(3) and also failed to examine the 2nd nomination paper and thus we are of the opinion that the case referred by the learned advocate for the respondent No. 7 reported in 62 DLR (AD) 425 has got no manner of application in the present case. Mr Azim further referred two other cases one is case ofAFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Hug, 41 DLR (AD) 63, the principle regarding non entertaining the writ application in election matters has been established by this judgment. Their Lordships in deciding 9 Civil Appeals and one Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal in the said case held that "the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution cannot be invoked except on the very limited ground of total absence of jurisdiction (coram non judice) or malice in law to challenge any step in the process of election including an order passed by the Election Commission under Rule 70 because (a) the real and larger issue of completion of free and fair election with rigorous promptitude for timely emergence and functioning of elective bodies must take precedence over settlement of private disputes. (b) all election disputes must wait pending completion of the election and be taken to the special forum created under the Election Law itself for their resolution, (c) almost invariably there will arise dispute over facts which cannot and should not be decided in an extra-ordinary and summary jurisdiction of writ." In this case their Lordships dealt with some disputes regarding Union Parishad Election. Their Lordships decided the Civil Appeal Nos. 40/98, 4/89, 2/89, 3/89, 38/88, 29/88, 17/89, 8/89 and Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 23/89. These all appeals were preferred against the judgment passed in the writ jurisdiction and their Lordships in the High Court Division in disposing the writ petition interfered with the decision of the Election Commission. The election commission had a power under Rule 70 to review any order passed by any officer under this Rule. The powers of the election commission under Rule 70 of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 (now nomitted) runs as follows: "70. Powers of Election Commission to issue orders.—Save as otherwise provided, the Election Commission may issue such instructions and exercise such powers, including the power to review an order passed by any officer under these Rules and make such consequential orders as may, in its opinion, be necessary for ensuring that an election is conducted honestly, justly and fairly and in accordance with the provisions of the Ordinance and these rules"

18. The High Court Division in disposing the cases against of which civil appeals were preferred interfered with the decision of the election commission, but in deciding the civil appeals their lordships in the Appellate Division held that "Election Commission has been given the power, from start to finish, to oversee that elections are held and conducted in accordance with law". Again their Lordships held that "Election Commission vested with plenary, supervisory and discretionary jurisdiction (i) to oversee that election is conducted honestly, justly, fairly and in accordance with the Ordinance & Rules made thereunder; (ii) to pass any order for repoll, acceptance/consolidation of result and review; (iii) Article 102 of the Constitution cannot be invoked except on the limited ground of coram non judice or malice in law." Facts of those cases are that, elections of the respective Union Parishad were held, after holding the election the election commission took some measures directing for holding elections or to hold election a fresh which were of course under the domain of the election commission. Deciding these matters the election commission had to examine facts, but the writ Court has no scope to assess any evidence. For this reason the Appellate Division of our Supreme Court interfered with the decision of the High Court Division. The fact of the case of AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Huq is totally different from that of the case in hand and thus the principle enunciated in this case has got no manner of application in the present case.

19. Mr Azim also referred the case of AKM Moyeedul Islam vs Bangladesh Election Commission, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 208, in this case the nomination paper of Hossain Mohammad Ershad was accepted by the Returning Officer and Mr Maidul Islam challenged the order of acceptance before the High Court Division and the High Court Division summarily rejected the writ petition. Against that order Mr Mayeedul Islam preferred civil appeal before the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, but their Lordships referring the decision of the case of AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Huq reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68 dismissed the appeal saying that "The High Court Division ought not to have prejudged the issue under Article 102 of the Constitution and ought not to have expressed any opinion on the issue. It ought to have rejected the writ petition in limine on the ground of maintainability, as no question of coram non judice or malice in law was raised in the writ petition."

20. By filing supplementary-affidavit Mr Fida M Kamal also agitated that the petitioner is not a loanee and has no liability with regard to any loan which has been certified by the Sonali Bank Limited, Nazirpur Branch, Pirojpur vide certificate dated 2-2-2014 and the Returning Officer as well as the appellate authority despite being aware of the said fact most illegally and with malafide intension cancelled the nomination paper of the petitioner, their action is tainted with malice in law and as such the impugned decision and order of cancellation of the nomination paper is absolutely illegal. Mr Fida Kamal submitted that the petitioner submitted some papers before the Returning Officer regarding the position of his loan, but both the Returning Officer and appellate authority the Deputy Commissioner, Pirojpur without considering the papers as submitted by the petitioner gave their decision cancelling one nomination paper of the petitioner which is of course is an action tainted with malice in law. Mr Azim also submits that the petitioner could have gone to the Election Tribunal to redress his grievance. Without going there he has invoked writ jurisdiction. Since as per the decision reported in 41 DLR (AD) 68 no writ petition can be entertained by this Court in sitting in the writ jurisdiction this writ petition is also not maintainable. In reply to this argument Mr Fida M Kamal submits that the Tribunal is only for the persons who are eligible to contest the election, no other persons can go to the Tribunal. Since the petitioner's nomination paper was cancelled and his name did not find any place to the list of valid candidates as published by the Returning Officer he did not have any scope to move to the Tribunal thus he had only alternative and efficacious remedy by filing writ petition before this Hon'ble Court challenging the impugned order.

21. Section 22(Ka) of the Upazila Parishad Ain, 1998 deals with election dispute and election Tribunal which runs as follows:

“২২ক। নির্বাচন বিরোধ, নির্বাচন ট্রাইব্যুনাল ইত্যাদি-

(১) এই আইনের অধীন কোন নির্বাচন কার্যক্রম সম্পর্কে নির্বাচন ট্রাইব্যুনাল ব্যতীত কোন আদালত বা অন্য কোন কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না।

(২) এই আইনের অধীন নির্বাচন সম্পর্কিত বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তির উদ্দেশ্যে নির্বাচন কমিশন, সাব-জজ পদমর্যাদার বিচার বিভাগীয় একজন কর্মকর্তা সমন্বয়ে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক নির্বাচন ট্রাইব্যুনাল এবং একজন জেলা জজ পদমর্যাদার বিচার বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা সমন্বয়ে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক নির্বাচন আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল গঠন করিতে হইবে।

(৩) কোন নির্বাচনের জন্য মনোনীত প্রার্থী সেই নির্বাচনের কোন বিষয়ে প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন ও প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা করিয়া নির্বাচন ট্রাইব্যুনালে দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন; অন্য কোন ব্যক্তি এইরুপ দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবে না।”

22. As per section 22(3) only a valid nominated candidate can raise any question regarding election process before the Tribunal; no other person/persons can file this kind of application before the Tribunal. As per Rule 55 only the contesting candidate can file election application before the Tribunal. The provision of Rule 55 of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 runs as follows:

“৫৫। নির্বাচনী দরখাস্ত-(১) আইনের ধারা ২২ক এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে উপ-বিধি (২) এর অধীন নির্বাচনী দরখাস্ত দাখিল ব্যতীত, নির্বাচন সম্পর্কে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না।

(২) কোন প্রতিদ্বন্ধী প্রার্থী যে নির্বাচনে প্রার্থী ছিলেন সেই নির্বাচন চ্যালেঞ্জ করিয়া দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন।”

23. As per Rule 2 (definition Clause 17) the contesting candidate means a candidate who has been validly nominated for contesting the election and has not withdrawn his nomination paper, the definition of contesting candidate (protidandi prarthi) runs as follows:

“প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বী প্রার্থী অর্থ এমন একজন প্রার্থী যিনি চেয়ারম্যান অথবা মহিলা সদস্য হিসাবে নির্বাচনের জন্য বৈধভাবে মনোনীত হইয়াছেন এবং যিনি তাহার প্রার্থীতা প্রত্যাহার করেন নাই।”

24. Since the petitioner's name was not placed in the list of valid candidates and his one nomination paper was cancelled by the Returning Officer as well as the appellate authority, the respondent No. 5, apparently as per provision of the Upazila Parishad Election Rules, 2013 the petitioner was not competent to go to the Election Tribunal as he was not a valid candidate or contesting candidate. Since the door of the Election Tribunal is closed for the petitioner and the petitioner had no other forum to ventilate his grievance, he moved this Court to invoke the writ jurisdiction to protect his right and, as such, we are of the view that this case is unlike to the cases referred by the respondents and we also hold that the writ Court is competent enough to entertain the writ application to scrutinize the order of the Returning Officer and his appellate authority as their decision is final as per Upazilla Election Rule, 2013.

25. Mr Fida M Kamal also submitted that the High Court Division by allowing the petitioner to contest the election wanted the election to be held by participation of the petitioner. They did not halt the election process. He also submitted that after issuance of the Rule the respondent No. 7 being added, moved to the Appellate Division, but their Lordships in the Appellate Division did not stay the ad-interim order passed by the High Court Division at the time of issuance of the Rule. It is also in the record that after expiry of c.ie year from the date of Rule issuing order the Rule automatically became infructuous and it stood discharged. When the petitioner was running from one door to another to restore the Rule to its original file and number the High Court Division did not entertain the application and expressed their view by their order dated 7-9-2015 to the effect that, there is no any scope to restore the Rule to its original file and number as it has died it's natural death by expiry of the period of one year as it was the condition of the Rule to get the same heard within this time. It appears to us that though the petitioner could not get the Rule heard in the stipulated time, but nevertheless the respondent No. 7 and other respondents also did not take any initiative to get the Rule heard within the said period. After rejection of the application for restoration of the Rule the petitioner moved before the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court against the said order. On our query Mr Fida M Kamal submitted that the respondents side raised the question of maintainability of writ petition before the Appellate Division and they referred the decision of 62 DLR (AD) 425, but from the order passed by the Appellate Division it is very clear that their Lordships did not find any merit in the submissions made by the learned advocate for the respondent No. 7 regarding maintainability of the writ petition, rather they found merit in the submissions of the learned advocate for the petitioner and their Lordships set-aside the judgment of the High Court Division dated 7-9-2015 rejecting the restoration application and restored the said Rule to its original file and number. From the Rule issuing order it appears that their Lordships in the High Court Division allowed the ball to role on the ground. They did not want to halt the election process, the Appellate Division also did not want to hold the new election as per the gazette notification dated 24-8-2015, rather they decided to get the Rule heard which was initially issued by this Division on 15-4-2014.

<u>26. The petitioner has challenged the gazette dated 24-8-2015 and has obtained a supplementary Rule from this Court. In disposing these two Rules, we are of the view that the writ petition against the rejection of the nomination paper is maintainable because the petitioner has invoked the writ jurisdiction against such an order which has been termed as 'Final'. The petitioner does/did not have any other alternative forum to get his grievance remedied. Thus, the writ jurisdiction is the only forum to see whether or not the Returning Officer as well as his appellate authority has performed their duty in accordance with law.</u>

<u>27. As per section 20 of the Upazilla Parishad Ain, 1998 (as amended up to 2014) and Rule 63 of Upazila Parishad Election Rule, 2013 the Election Commission has power to conduct election and also has power to make Rules. According to rule 3 of the Upazila Election Rule 2013 the Election Commission has some power to conduct the Upazila Election. The Election Commission under the provision of rule 17 has given the power to the Returning Officer to scrutinize the nomination paper of any candidate and to give decision thereupon. Under the provision of rule 18(3), the Election Commission can appoint any officer of the republic as the appellate authority of the Returning Officer. As per rule 18(4), an unfettered power has been given to the appellate authority, who is nothing but a government employee. Rule 18(4) has given this government employee a power to allow or dismiss any appeal, this decision of the appellate authority has been described/termed as final. Even the constitutional body 'The Election Commission' has no any power to interfere with the decision of the appellate authority. Such an unguarded power of the appellate authority who is nothing, but a government servant is against the principles of rule of law, we emphasize.</u>

28. Since every executive order passed by any authority of the executive organ of the republic is amenable in writ jurisdiction the unguarded and unfettered power of the appellate authority of the Returning Officer of Upazilla Election who is also a government servant cannot escape the clutch of the test of judicial review. Thus in our view, challenging any order whether it relates to acceptance or rejection of the nomination paper of any candidate in Upazila Parishad Election by the appellate authority before the High Court Division under writ jurisdiction is maintainable.

<u>29. We are also of the view that non-examination of any nomination paper is illegal as it violates the mandatory provision of rule 17(4) of the rule 2013. The returning officer must record his opinion on each and every nomination paper as per rule 17(4). Failing to do so the non-scrutinized nomination paper cannot be considered as invalid rather it should be treated as a valid one. Not giving any specific and reasoned decision on any nomination paper filed by any candidate the status of the same should be considered as valid one; cancellation of one nomination paper does not ipso facto invalidate the other nomination paper as per Rule (অ).</u>

30. We are also of the view that the High Court Division considering this aspect without staying the order passed by the Returning Officer and the appellate authority on 9-2-2014 passed the 2nd portion of the Rule issuing order and directed the respondents to allow the petitioner to participate in the election. If at the time of issuing the Rule the High Court Division had stayed the impugned order dated 9-2-2014 the petitioner could have participated in the election, but without doing so the High Court Division issued the 2nd part of the Rule issuing order.

31. We have also observed that in this case although government and election commission has been made as respondent’s No. 1 to 6, but none of these respondents appeared before this Court to contest the Rule. Presumably, it can be said that they did not have any grievance as the petitioner was allowed to contest the election as per order of the High Court Division and the voters of the Nazirpur Upazila who are the ultimate judge of the election runners have elected the petitioner as Upazila Chairman and he has been functioning as the Chairman of the said Parishad. Perhaps the said respondents thought that it would be better not to contest the Rule, but nevertheless the respondent No. 7 or any respondent was not precluded to come to the Court to provide assistance to arrive a correct decision.

32. In the above circumstances, we are of the view that the decisions given by the Returning Officer and his appellate authority, the respondent No. 6 and 5 respectively rejecting the nomination paper of the petitioner are tainted with malice in law and the act of non-examining the 2nd nomination paper of the petitioner is illegal and this inaction gave the petitioner a status of a valid candidate. We find merit in the submissions advanced by Mr Fida M Kamal.

33. Accordingly both the Rules are made absolute.

Let a copy of this judgment be communicated at once.

End.
